sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Blocks, procs, and lambdas are the most distinctively Ruby topic in any backend interview, and the one candidates most often get half-right. The four key differences between a Proc and a lambda — return behaviour, arity enforcement, the === operator, and lambda? — appear in almost every mid-level Ruby interview. This page covers the full picture: block syntax (do/end vs curly brace precedence), yield and block_given?, converting methods to procs with &method(:name), the stabby lambda syntax, closures and captured bindings, Proc#curry for partial application, and how Enumerable builds its entire API on top of a single block expectation. Every answer includes the idiomatic Ruby pattern — no verbose Java-style explicit returns.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: blocks-and-yield, proc-vs-lambda, closures-currying, functional-patterns. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
